texts: The cauldrons come to a slow boil.
Hesper keeps the cauldrons at a steady simmer.
A hard boil ruins the distillation.
A hard boil yields a thin slick of poor essence.
The threads dissolve slowly through the afternoon.
By late afternoon a dark slick forms at the bottom of each cauldron.
The slick is the precursor of mire-essence.

fields.sentence: The cauldrons come to a slow boil.
parse: (: cauldron_boil_rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_group_1) (And (Member (sk_come $x) come) (Patient (sk_come $x) $x) (Member (sk_boil $x) boil) (Experiencer (sk_boil $x) $x) (Member (sk_boil $x) slow) (Member $x boil) (Result (sk_come $x) (sk_boil $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The top-level group "come" event (statements 1-2) carries no Result link and no result state, so at group level the parse asserts only that the cauldrons "came" — reading as motion — with "to a slow boil" recoverable solely from inside the per-member rule.

q2_gaps: light-verb change-of-state "come to a <state noun>" — the change-of-kind/phase rule names only "became" / "turned into" / "turned ADJ" and the idiom rule is a coherence test, so nothing decides between a fixed idiom symbol (come_to_a_boil) and the become-pattern the parse used; under that pattern the mandatory flat dual-emit yields (Member $x boil), i.e. each cauldron IS a boil
review.notes: Definite plural -> group plus per-member distribution rule, Patient on the change-of-state subject, and the absent tense atom on the bare simple present are all correct. Whether "a slow boil" licenses the Skolem-function state variant of the resultative group rule (reserved for states carrying their own per-member complement) is marginal — "slow" is a modifier, not a complement.

issues.reason: The plural-bearer resultative rule hands only the FLAT half to the per-member rule, "beside the reified result state", so the group level must still carry the reified boil state and (Result sk_come_1 sk_boil_1); as emitted, the only top-level claim about the cauldrons is an unqualified come event, and Core patterns forbids dropping a stated restriction — omitting "to a slow boil" there widens the claim.

gaps_confirmed: nothing decides between a fixed idiom symbol (come_to_a_boil) and the change-of-kind/phase State-result pattern for "come to a <state noun>" — the phase rule names only became / turned into / turned ADJ, and the idiom rule is a coherence test; and under the phase pattern the mandatory flat dual-emit yields the FALSE atom (Member $x boil), i.e. each cauldron IS a boil
new_gaps: the plural note under Resultatives is written for a plural OBJECT; in a change of phase the state's bearer is the SUBJECT, and nothing states whether the reified result state may then take the group as its Experiencer or must be minted per member
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form keeps the resultative at group level — the come event plus the reified (Member sk_boil_1 boil) (Experiencer sk_boil_1 sk_group_1) (Member sk_boil_1 slow) state and (Result sk_come_1 sk_boil_1) — handing only the flat half to the per-member rule; but no fully compliant form exists, because that flat half is (Member $x boil), which is false of a cauldron, so this sentence's result cannot be recorded without either dropping it at group level or asserting a falsehood.
adjudication.notes: Definite plural to group witness, Patient on the change-of-state subject, "slow" split as incidental description rather than fused, and the absent tense atom on the bare simple present are all correct.

fields.sentence: Hesper keeps the cauldrons at a steady simmer.

q2_gaps: A maintenance resultative whose result state is a PP-expressed nominal eventuality ("keeps the cauldrons at a steady simmer"): the State-result shape and its mandated flat half are stated only for adjectival results ("kept the gate shut"), so applying them mechanically to a state noun yields a flat/per-member atom that types the object as the state noun itself, (Member $x simmer).
review.notes: The parse applies the maintenance-resultative doctrine as written — Theme object, reified state with Still, Result link, the plural group's flat half replaced by the per-member (PartOf $x g) rule at STV 1.0 0.9, and no status atom on the habitual present; the awkward per-member conclusion is the doctrine's own shape, not a parser choice.

fields.sentence: A hard boil ruins the distillation.

review.notes: The indefinite subject correctly stays a witness (a verbal generic needs a bare plural or an explicit quantifier, not "a"), hard_boil exposes both its head genus and its gradable-adjective modifier, "the distillation" is a first-mention definite witness, and ruin takes Agent on the inanimate transitive subject plus Patient on the destroyed object, with no status atom for the habitual reading.

fields.sentence: A hard boil yields a thin slick of poor essence.

q1_issues.issue: "poor" modifies the mass noun "essence", not the slick, but it is emitted as a property of sk_slick_1.
The of-phrase is collapsed into identity typing on the slick's own symbol, so the essence gets no referent of its own and no atom records that the slick is a portion OF essence.

q2_gaps: A portion/quantity noun taking a bare-MASS "of"-phrase ("a thin slick of poor essence" - the "a cup of water" shape): the genitive rule explicitly excludes it from Possession as a measure, the partitive/mass route needs a definite whole for PartOf and ProportionOf, and Measure needs a stated magnitude and unit, so no encoding is specified for it.
review.notes: The rest is right: an indefinite subject with a verbal predicate takes a witness rather than a generic, the inanimate transitive subject stays Agent, and yield creates its object so Patient is correct.

issues.reason: The atom is true of the sentence's content given the parse's own (Member sk_slick_1 essence): the slick IS the poor essence, so predicating poor of it asserts nothing the text denies — and the objection is to improvisation in territory the instruction set leaves uncovered, since it excludes a measure of-phrase ("a cup of water") from Possession without supplying a replacement.

This mistakes a coverage gap for a defect: no head is licensed for an INDEFINITE portion of-phrase (PartOf's mass-partitive use needs a definite whole, Possession is explicitly barred for a measure), and the typing chosen mirrors the licensed Partitives shape "a part of a homogeneous mass is still that mass" — every emitted atom is true and well-typed, and nothing is missing that the instruction set requires.

gaps_confirmed: A portion / quantity noun with a bare-MASS of-phrase ("a thin slick of poor essence", the "a cup of water" shape) has no licensed encoding: Possession is explicitly excluded for a measure, the mass-partitive PartOf / ProportionOf route needs a definite whole, and Measure needs a stated magnitude and unit.
new_gaps: With no head for the portion relation, the of-phrase's own modifier ("poor") has nowhere to attach except the portion's symbol, so a scope distinction the sentence makes — "thin" on the slick, "poor" on the essence — is unrecoverable in any licensed form; a licensed encoding would need to carry the mass referent and its modifiers separately from the portion's.
adjudication.notes: The remaining atoms hold: the indefinite subject of a verbal predicate takes a witness rather than a generic, the inanimate transitive subject stays Agent, yield brings its object into existence so Patient is right, and the habitual present correctly carries no status atom. Fusing hard_boil (term-of-art reading) and exposing its gradable modifier genus is a judgment call the compound rules permit.

fields.sentence: The threads dissolve slowly through the afternoon.

q2_gaps: durative 'through/over the <period>' frame ('through the afternoon'): During is licensed only for during/while/throughout, Measure duration needs a stated count, and Start/End need stated terms, so the extent sense has no carrier and collapses onto the point-like day-part (Time e afternoon)
review.notes: Definite plural to group witness, dissolve as change-of-state Patient, -ly manner adverb kept in surface form, and the group event plus per-member distribution rule at 1.0/0.9 all follow doctrine.

fields.sentence: By late afternoon a dark slick forms at the bottom of each cauldron.
parse: (: cauldron_slick_rule (Implication (Member $x cauldron) (And (Member (sk_form $x) form) (Patient (sk_form $x) (sk_slick $x)) (Member (sk_slick $x) slick) (Member (sk_slick $x) dark) (Location (sk_form $x) (sk_bottom $x)) (PartOf (sk_bottom $x) $x) (Member (sk_bottom $x) bottom) (TimeAtMost (sk_form $x) late_afternoon))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q2_gaps: a MODIFIED day-part time constant ('late afternoon') — the day-part inventory covers bare morning/afternoon/evening/night and the bound-term list dawn/noon/dusk/night, and nothing says whether a modified day-part becomes one constant (late_afternoon), takes compound decomposition like a modifier+noun kind, or is unrepresentable
review.notes: The universal 'each cauldron' takes the kind-ranging rule with 1.0/0.9 and its QuantifierPhrase companion, the indefinite slick and the cauldron's bottom are dependent Skolem functions of $x, 'by <time>' is the deadline TimeAtMost, and the creation event carries Location with no LocatedIn on the created slick — all as the instruction set specifies.

fields.sentence: The slick is the precursor of mire-essence.

q1_issues.issue: "Precursor of" is a true relational noun (the "tributary of the river" case), so *Complements of nouns and adjectives* routes its of-phrase to the ordinary genitive Possession; the nominalization-object Of oblique is reserved for a head noun naming an act, result or quality whose own underlying verb takes the of-NP as object, which "precursor" is not.

review.notes: The call is genuinely close - "the precursor of X" paraphrases as "what precedes X" - but "precursor" is not deverbal in English, so the relational-noun clause should govern; Of is a licensed head, just the wrong one of the two routes here. Everything else (witness for the definite singular, Member for the predicate nominal on an individual, mire_essence genus, no uniqueness atom for "the") follows the instruction set.

issues.reason: The stated verb-paraphrase test routes 'the N of X' to the entity-attached `Of` oblique only when the head noun has its own underlying verb taking the of-NP as object; 'precursor' has none (English has no verb 'precurse'), so it is the 'capital of' / 'a tributary of the river' relational-noun case the instruction set assigns to the ordinary opaque genitive `Possession`.

adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form replaces `(Of sk_slick_1 mire_essence)` with `(Possession sk_slick_1 mire_essence)` — possessed first, opaque, covering the loose relational link without meaning ownership — leaving the other three atoms unchanged.
adjudication.notes: The call is close, but the route has a consequence the instruction set names explicitly (possession questions always query the `Possession` form regardless of how the fact was stated), so the wrong route makes the link unfindable rather than merely differently worded. Everything else — witness for the definite singular, `Member` for the predicate nominal on an individual, the `mire_essence` genus — follows the instruction set.
